# Web design

Rules for pages and web apps, judged on what renders. Pair this with the embedded `frontend-design` guidance, which owns the visual direction; this skill adds the systems, the semantics and the capture floor.

## Shared core

Judge every rule on the rendered result, from the captures; the rules under Direction before code are the exception, checked as a plan in the worker's report or `DESIGN.md`, not on a render. `(behavior check)` marks a rule no capture can show (a file, a process, an input sequence): Worker.operations runs it and reports it, and nobody infers it from a still. `(preference)` marks taste: list it, do not repair it. A violation of any other rule is judged by this definition:

A discrepancy is material, and starts a repair whatever its size, when it affects acceptance, hierarchy or composition, legibility (cramped, overlapping, clipped or disappearing text), responsiveness at a viewport or size the criteria list, whether text and numbers state the content correctly (a title that misstates what it covers), accessibility, interaction correctness, adherence to a reference or obvious production quality; unnecessary text, headings, cards or badges are design defects. Only pure preference, with none of these effects, stays unrepaired: list it apart, marked optional.

A number is binding only where a platform guideline fixes it; every other number is a default, marked `(default)`, that the design may override with a stated reason.

### Direction before code

- Name the subject, the audience and the main job, and propose them when the brief omits them. The brief's own words outrank every avoid list below.
- Write a compact plan before building: palette roles, type roles, a layout concept and two or three principles. Test it with "would I make this for any similar product?" and the competitor test: drop an idea that still works with a competitor's name on it.
- Say whether this is a refinement, which preserves the existing design, or a redesign, which replaces it.

### Platform fidelity over invention

- Use the platform's own components, navigation and conventions unless the brief gives a reason not to, and brand through the layer the platform leaves open.
- Ported-from-a-website test: a fluent user of the platform never pauses at an off-spec control.
- Rules here are platform concepts. Detect the project's stack and map each rule onto it; never assume one.

### Design record

- Read `DESIGN.md` at the project root before UI work and create or update it after: platform and stack, direction, color roles, type roles, spacing and shape, components and states, do and don't. Note a changed decision instead of silently overwriting it. (behavior check)

### Spend boldness in one place

- One signature detail per screen, and remove one accessory before finishing. Replace removed ornament with scale, real content or a real image, so the screen is not left thin. (preference)
- A labeled gray placeholder beats drawn art or emoji used as icons. (preference)

### Quality floor, unannounced

- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and non-text control contrast at least 3:1. Color is never the only signal.
- Every state exists and is captured where reachable: hover or press, focus, disabled, loading, empty, error and long content.
- The system's reduced-motion, larger-text and high-contrast settings, where the platform has them, change the render.
- Copy uses the user's words, specific verbs and one name per action, and an error says how to fix it.

## Web rules

- Name the mode in the plan. An expressive page (marketing, editorial) is judged on point of view and composition; a task-oriented product UI is judged on familiarity and speed of use. (preference)
- A product UI earns familiarity: one type family, motion of about 150 to 250 ms only as feedback to an action, no page-load choreography, and a modal only as a last resort. (default)

### Systems, not values

- Space, type size, shadow and opacity come from small scales. For space, for example 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 96, with no adjacent steps closer than about 25%. Symptom: near-identical gaps or one-off sizes in the capture. (default)
- More space surrounds a group than sits inside it, so groups read at a glance.
- Two font weights. Hierarchy comes from weight and color before size, with at most three text colors. (default)
- The layout holds its hierarchy in grayscale before color is added. (preference)
- Body text measure is 65 to 75 characters, and a line never spans a wide screen. (default)

### Actions and hierarchy

- One primary action per view, visibly dominant over the rest.
- A destructive action is not a big red button by default; the strong styling sits inside its confirmation. Capture the confirmation step.
- Destructive actions are confirmed or undoable. (behavior check)

### Semantics and input

- Buttons act and links navigate. A control that navigates is a link and one that acts is a button. (behavior check)
- Icon-only buttons have an accessible label, and a tooltip on hover and focus where a pointer exists.
- Focus is visible on every interactive element in a keyboard traversal. An outline is never removed without a visible replacement.
- Forms accept paste, use the input type and autofill hint that fit each field, and never block the user. (behavior check)
- After a failed submit, each error sits inline beside its field and focus moves to the first one. Capture that frame.

### Content edge cases

- Truncation, long words, an empty state and very long content render without overflow, overlap or a broken layout.
- State that should survive a reload or a share lives in the URL: reload and open the copied URL fresh, and the same view returns. (behavior check)

### Motion

- Only transform and opacity animate, never a blanket "all properties" transition. (behavior check)
- Animations can be interrupted, and under reduced motion movement is replaced by a fade or nothing. Capture with the setting on.

### Themed browser surfaces

- Selection color, caret, scrollbars and focus rings are styled as part of the design in both themes.

## Refuse list

Unless the brief asks for it:

- identical icon-card grids and hero metric tiles
- an eyebrow label over every heading
- gradient text and side-stripe borders
- glass as decoration (preference)
- emoji as icons
- "01 / 02 / 03" numbering without a real sequence
- cream with terracotta, or near-black with an acid accent (preference)

## Capture checklist

Capture at phone, tablet and desktop widths. For each, capture light and dark, reduced motion on, and 200% text zoom; also a keyboard-only focus traversal, each state of the key control, the confirmation of a destructive action and a failed form submit.

Apply it on the final captures: the worker before reporting, the reviewer in its findings and the root in its own final pass. Report only checks actually run, and name each check not run.
